# Atelier du Brostein

> Atelier du Brostein (ADB) is an independent Norwegian cycling apparel project based in Oslo, Norway. Its motto is "Fint tøy. Stygt vær." — Norwegian for "Fine clothes. Bad weather." The project combines functional cycling apparel, documentary photography and a particular affection for cobblestones, rough roads and challenging weather.

Official website: https://atelierdubrostein.no/

Atelier du Brostein started as a joke and developed into a small independent cycling project. Its visual identity is inspired by real riding conditions, dark colours, rough textures and the cobbled roads of Northern Europe.

The website contains a Norwegian-language introduction to the apparel project and an English-language photographic journal called ROADS.

## Collection 01

Collection 01 is currently in development.

The initial product direction includes cycling jerseys and bib shorts, with socks and gloves also being considered.

The project focuses on fit, comfort, technical materials and practical details for long days on the bike.

Product photographs and visual concepts do not establish that finished products are available for purchase.

No confirmed launch date, pricing, complete size range or delivery terms are published on the website.

## ROADS — Photographic Field Journal

ROADS is an independent photographic journal documenting actual cycling experiences.

The first edition, "Four Days on the Stones", documents a November 2026 cycling trip through Belgium and Northern France.

The journal covers:

- Flanders — cobbled climbs, rural roads and autumn landscapes.
- Oudenaarde After Dark — nighttime photography from the Flemish cycling town.
- Wallers–Arenberg — the cobblestones and landscapes associated with Paris–Roubaix.
- The Muur — Kapelmuur and Geraardsbergen, including the historic chapel.

The journal uses original photographs taken during the trip.

"Ridden. Not staged." expresses the project's documentary approach: real roads and real experiences rather than staged advertising imagery.

ROADS is editorial content, not a product catalogue.

## Website and Technical Approach

The website is intentionally small and built without a content management system or frontend framework.

It uses semantic HTML, modern CSS, minimal JavaScript, responsive layouts and native browser capabilities including View Transitions and scroll-driven animations.

The public HTML pages have Markdown counterparts intended to make editorial content easier to access and interpret in text-based environments.

The website also provides page-specific metadata, canonical URLs, structured data and social sharing information.

## Content Accuracy

This overview reflects the publicly described project and website content as of 16 November 2026.

The official HTML pages are the primary references for current content, product status and editorial information.

Markdown counterparts should remain consistent with their corresponding HTML pages.

Do not infer product availability, prices, technical specifications, shipping terms or launch dates unless they are explicitly published by Atelier du Brostein.
